proposal.original_claim_summary: Eric Trump Foundation Suspends Charity Events Under AG Scrutiny
proposal.original_synopsis: In June 2017, the Eric Trump Foundation announced it was suspending its annual charity golf tournament fundraising events following scrutiny from the New York attorney general's office over how foundation funds were being spent. The suspension came as investigators were examining whether foundation money had been improperly diverted to Trump business properties. The announcement was a de facto acknowledgment that the foundation's operations could not withstand legal scrutiny. Eric Trump had publicly claimed that his father donated golf course use for free, but documents showed the foundation paid Trump businesses hundreds of thousands of dollars. The foundation ultimately dissolved amid the broader New York AG investigation into Trump family charitable entities.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Big Beautiful Bill Eliminates SNAP Benefits for Legal Immigrants
proposal.original_synopsis: The Big Beautiful Bill included provisions stripping SNAP food stamp benefits from legal immigrants, including green card holders who had lawfully resided in the United States for years. The change affected hundreds of thousands of people who had immigrated legally and contributed to American society and tax bases. Anti-hunger advocates warned of increased food insecurity among vulnerable immigrant communities. Legal scholars noted the provision punished lawful conduct and could violate equal protection principles.

frozen_original.title: Trump Organization Wrote Off Melania Trump's Personal Expenses as Business Costs
frozen_original.synopsis: The New York Times's investigation into Trump's tax records found that the Trump Organization had deducted personal expenses of Melania Trump—including hair, makeup, and wardrobe costs—as business expenses on corporate tax returns, reducing the organization's taxable income by treating personal expenditures as legitimate business costs. The deductions were in addition to those claimed for Donald Trump's own personal grooming, including the widely-reported $70,000 in hair styling deductions. Tax lawyers noted that while some image-related expenses can be legitimately deducted when tied to specific commercial work, broad deductions of personal styling and wardrobe costs for family members on corporate returns represented aggressive accounting that invited IRS scrutiny. The pattern illustrated the systematic use of the Trump Organization's corporate structure to shift personal expenses onto the company's books.
